claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex, who's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19 years old, I need to ask about his current situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as university, college, vocational training, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education, which is important for eligibility.

Now I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to ask about your residency status and circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. I have most of the information I need. Just one more question to complete the assessment:

**Are you, or is your partner (if you have one), receiving any of the following benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither I nor my partner receive any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your circumstances:
- You have one child: Alex, who is 19 years old
- Alex is in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You live in the UK
- You're not receiving Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit

Based on the Child Benefit rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. However, there's a special provision for children aged 16-19: you'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 19 and in approved education (A-levels), he meets the criteria for continued eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex is 19, you can still claim Child Benefit for him because he is under 20 and remains in approved education (A-levels). This extended eligibility applies as long as he continues in his approved education.

If Alex leaves his education or training, you would need to inform HMRC, as your eligibility may change. However, if he leaves and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?

Under Child Benefit rules for children aged 16 or over, eligibility continues if the child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training. Alex meets both criteria: he is under 20 and is currently in approved education. The claimant lives with Alex in the UK and is not receiving disqualifying benefits.
